correctness.rationale: Read exact Kenyon--Prause Section 3.4 boundary s(R)=avg_i a_i/(R+a_i), t(R)=avg_j R/(R+c_j), a_i=alpha_i^2<c_j=beta_j^-2 (R>0). s strictly decreases from 1 to 0; t increases 0 to 1; a_i<c_j ensures t(R)<1-s(R) so the curve bounds a genuine area against s+t=1. By orientation area=1/2-int_0^1 T(s)ds=1/2-int_0^infty t(R)(-s'(R))dR. Expansion gives ordered pair integrals int_0^infty [R/(R+c_j)] [a_i/(R+a_i)^2] dR. Setting R=a_i x, q=a_i/c_j reduces to I(q)=int_0^infty qx/((1+qx)(1+x)^2) dx = q/(q-1)-q log(q)/(q-1)^2. F(q)=1/2-I(q), matching asserted formula for all m1,m2. Independently evaluated exact integral numerically for q=.01,.1,.5,.9, obtaining F approximately .4631142722,.3268413465,.11370563888,.0175535908, equal to closed form within quadrature precision; analytic separation, not quadrature, proves arbitrary periods.

value.rationale: The coexistence region has a natural geometric size in the model's physically meaningful slope simplex. Despite nontrivial higher-period boundary dependence, its area reduces exactly to the arithmetic mean of universal one-cell contributions, giving a reusable global invariant across arbitrary periods and a precise way to compare environments without reconstructing the full phase curve. This is more than a cosmetic simplification of a previously evaluated scalar.

final_claim: For a strictly small-r genus-zero m1-by-m2 periodic five-vertex system with alpha_i beta_j<1 for every pair, the Euclidean area in source slope coordinates between diagonal s+t=1 and the Kenyon--Prause small-r coexistence curve is exactly (1/(m1 m2))*sum_{i,j} F((alpha_i beta_j)^2), with F(q)=[1-q^2+2q log q]/[2(1-q)^2]. This gives the all-period cellwise-averaging identity.
limitations: Strict all-products alpha_i beta_j<1 small-r genus-zero setting only, Euclidean slope-coordinate area; no q=1 or large-r assertion.
Finite quadrature is supporting evidence only; analytic integral proves unrestricted finite-period identity.
